newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-GRAF BEATS OLYMPIC CHAMP DAVENPORT IN 13-11 TIE-BREAK.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GRAF BEATS OLYMPIC CHAMP DAVENPORT IN 13-11 TIE-BREAK.

text.p: World number one Steffi Graf won a thrilling 13-11 final-set tiebreaker over Olympic champion Lindsay Davenport on Thursday to reach the semifinals of the $2 million WTA Tour Chase Championships.

Defending champion Graf, pressured by the booming groundstrokes of the big American, overcame deficits in each set to score a 6-4 7-6 victory that took one hour 40 minutes on the blue carpet at Madison Square Garden.
Graf faced triple set point at 3-6 in the tie-break before pulling off her best escape, rattling off three winners in a row to extend the tension-packed decider.
A third successive groundstroke error by the weary Davenport finally put Graf over the top on her fourth match point of the climactic tiebreaker, in which Davenport squandered five set points.

"I was a little nervous at the start," said Graf, who showed no ill effects from the back ailment that forced her to quit last Sunday's final in Philadelphia. "Maybe I needed to be trailing to come back and focus."

Unseeded Croatian Iva Majoli used a pair of tiebreakers to take her place in the final four of the elite, season-ending championship by beating fourth seed Conchita Martinez of Spain 7-6 (8-6) 7-6 (7-4) in a tumultuous two-hour 12-minute match.
First Martinez got into hot water with a warning from umpire Missy Malool for kicking her racket over a disputed line call in the first-set tiebreaker.
That was followed by a point-penalty for visible obscenity in the first game of the second set, putting the Spaniard one more violation away from disqualification.

Then at 2-2 in the second set, Majoli suddenly had trouble breathing and summoned tour trainer Kathleen Stroia, who administered a lengthy examination before treating her for a rib problem during an injury timeout.
Majoli returned and held on to beat Martinez, who was herself treated for a hamstring injury in her win Wednesday.
Despite her own recent injury woes, Graf won her hard-hitting battle against Davenport largely on superior quickness and fitness.
"I felt pretty good," Graf said. "The last few weeks I didn't move too much and today I had to move a lot. I'm a little tired now, but I feel good that I was able to do it."
Davenport, whose victory over Graf in the semifinals this year in Los Angeles was one of only four defeats suffered by the German all season, was disappointed.
"I don't think I played my best," said Davenport. "Today, every big point I played terrible."
Graf improved her record to 5-1 against Davenport, but once again was hard-pressed by the big right-hander.
"She's very dangerous," said Graf. "She's a player who plays like me. She's pretty aggressive and puts me immediately on the defensive which I'm not used to."
Davenport said: "I don't think she likes it when someone hits the ball hard and she has to step back."
The top-seeded Graf was a break down twice during the first set before breaking Davenport's serve three straight times at the end to prevail 6-4 over 47 hard-fought minutes.
Davenport, able to put Graf on the defensive with her hard, flat groundstrokes, broke Graf twice in the second set to grab a 5-2 lead before the German charged back.
Graf shut Davenport down, holding her to five points over the next four games in taking a 6-5 lead.
But the ebb and flow of the entertaining match continued as eighth-seeded Davenport rebounded to hold serve in the 12th game with a forehand winner that forced a tiebreaker.
Riding a new wave of momentum, Davenport seized a 6-3 lead in the tie-break to hold triple set point.

Davenport then unleashed a huge first serve that Graf wondrously returned with a backhand lunge and the German saved the set with a deep drop shot that left the Olympic champion staring at the ball, flat-footed at the baseline.
A forehand winner saved another set point for Graf, who then levelled the tie-break 6-6 with a blistering ace.
The see-saw tiebreaker was marked by long, sizzling rallies until Davenport ran out of steam at the finish.

"It's been a great year but not a great end of the year," said Davenport, who reached just one semifinal in her last seven tournaments. "But the gold medal in Atlanta was my dream come true and I'll always have that."
Graf advanced to Saturday's semifinals against the winner of Friday's match between Arantxa Sanchez Vicario and Jana Novotna.
Majoli, 19, meets the winner of the quarter-final between 16-year-old Martina Hingis of Switzerland and Japan's Kimiko Date, still one defeat away from formally entering retirement.
